question_interpretation: Under what conditions a prescription device is exempt from the section 502(f)(1) adequate-directions-for-use requirement.

issues.detail: 'Advertising conditions' is not a condition in 801.109. Advertising comes up only inside (c) and (d): the information for use must cover 'all purposes for which it is advertised or represented'. 801.109 has no separate condition on advertising, so a grader could wrongly expect advertising-control content.

J omits conditions that 801.109 imposes. (a): the device is held by persons lawfully in the trade or by a licensed practitioner, and is sold only to or on the order of a practitioner. (b)(2): the label states the method of application or use; surgical instruments are excluded from (b). (c): dispensing-package information, with the proviso for information commonly known to practitioners. (e): issuance or latest-revision date on labeling other than labels and cartons.
21 CFR 801.110 gives the related retail exemption at delivery to the ultimate user. It is optional for this question.
'Labeling limited to practitioner use' is a loose paraphrase of 801.109(a)(2): the device is to be sold only to, or on the prescription or other order of, a licensed practitioner.

explanation: The citation 801.109 is right. J captures the Rx-only statement and the adequate information for practitioners. It omits the possession/sale condition, the method-of-use label statement, and the labeling revision-date condition. It also adds 'advertising conditions', which the section does not contain as a separate condition.
proposed_corrected_answer: 21 CFR 801.109: a device that is not safe except under a licensed practitioner's supervision is exempt from 502(f)(1) only if all of the following conditions are met. (a) It is held by persons lawfully engaged in its manufacture, transport, storage or distribution, or by a licensed practitioner, and is to be sold only to or on the prescription or order of a practitioner. (b) Except for surgical instruments, the label bears 'Rx only' / '℞ only' or the 'Caution: Federal law restricts this device to sale by or on the order of a ___' statement, plus the method of application or use. (c) Labeling on or within the dispensing package gives practitioners information for use (indications, effects, routes, methods, frequency and duration, hazards, contraindications, side effects, precautions). This may be omitted if it is commonly known to practitioners. (d) Any other labeling that furnishes information for use contains adequate information for that use; reminder labeling is excepted. (e) Labeling other than labels and cartons bears the issuance or latest-revision date. 801.110 covers the retail delivery exemption.

question_interpretation: What information a labeler must submit to GUDID, and the deadline for submitting and updating it.

issues.detail: The timeframe the question asks about is in 21 CFR 830.330 ('Times for submission of unique device identification information'), which G does not cite. 830.300, 830.310 and 830.320 contain no deadline. A complete, correctly cited answer would cite 830.330 and get no credit for it under this key.

J's 'timeframe tied to the labeling date' is imprecise. 830.330(a) sets the deadline as no later than the date the label must bear a UDI under 801.20, i.e. the UDI compliance date, not the date of labeling. 830.330(b) requires updates whenever the information changes: by the date a device is first labeled with the changed information, or within 10 business days of the change if the information is not on the label.
830.320 also requires designating a contact for device identification and electronic GUDID submission, with a waiver route. J does not mention these.

explanation: 830.300 (devices subject) and 830.310 (the data elements) are correctly cited. 830.320 is the submission-mechanics section. The deadline is in 830.330, which G omits. J also misstates the trigger as the 'labeling date' instead of the 801.20 UDI compliance date, and omits the update timing.
proposed_corrected_answer: Scope (830.300): the labeler must submit for each version or model required to bear a UDI. Content (830.310): labeler name, contact and issuing agency(ies); the device identifier; any prior device identifier; direct-mark DI information; brand name; version or model; sterility; natural rubber latex; MRI safety; size; production-identifier types; premarket submission number or exemption; listing number; GMDN term or code; quantity per package. Mechanics (830.320): designated contact; electronic submission to GUDID unless a waiver applies. Timing (830.330): (a) no later than the date the label must bear a UDI under 801.20; (b) updates whenever information changes, no later than the date a device is first labeled with the changed information, or within 10 business days of the change if the information does not appear on the label.

question_interpretation: What 21 CFR 201 requires about the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer or distributor on a drug label.

issues.detail: Most of 201.1 is about who may be represented as 'manufacturer', and J leaves it out. Paragraph (b) requires the person to perform all listed operations; (c) and (d) give the alternatives when operations are contracted out; (e) defines performing an operation; (f) requires the name to match the registered establishment name. Under (h)(2), an unqualified name is a representation that the person is the sole manufacturer and misbrands the product if untrue.

J omits the scope limits. 201.1(a) does not apply to drugs dispensed under 503(b)(1), and 201.1(m) excludes biological products subject to PHS Act 351. It also omits the place-of-business content in 201.1(i) (street address, city, State, ZIP; country for foreign manufacturers).
The distributor-qualifier element is right. 201.1(h)(5) lists the permitted phrases, such as 'Manufactured for', 'Distributed by' and 'Marketed by'; 201.1(h)(6) covers 'Packed by'.

explanation: G (201.1) is correct and both J elements are supported by 201.1(a) and (h)(5). Unlike its device counterpart 801.1, however, 201.1 mainly regulates who may be named as manufacturer, and a misrepresentation is misbranding. J omits that and the scope exclusions, which matter for a complete answer.
proposed_corrected_answer: 21 CFR 201.1: (a) a drug in finished package form must bear conspicuously the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer or distributor; this does not apply to drugs dispensed under 503(b)(1), and (m) excludes PHS Act 351 biologics. (b)-(f): who may be represented as manufacturer is the person performing all listed operations, with the (c)/(d) alternatives for contracted operations, and the name must match the registered establishment name. (g): actual corporate name. (h): an unqualified name means sole manufacturer; a distributor must be qualified ('Manufactured for', 'Distributed by', etc.) and a packer by 'Packed by'. (i): place of business is street address, city, State and ZIP (country for foreign). (j): principal place of business allowed unless misleading.

question_interpretation: How the net quantity of contents must be declared on a drug label (the question does not limit itself to OTC or prescription).

issues.detail: 21 CFR 201.62 applies only to over-the-counter drugs: it is in Subpart C, and 201.62(a) reads 'The label of an over-the-counter drug in package form'. Net quantity for prescription and insulin-containing drugs is governed by 21 CFR 201.51 (Subpart B). The key cites only 201.62 for an unqualified 'drug label' question.

J's 'placement ... and prominence' elements are OTC-specific: principal display panel placement, separation, boldface and minimum type heights by PDP area in 201.62(d)-(h). 201.51 for Rx drugs has no PDP placement or type-height rules; it requires the declaration to appear as a distinct item on the label. Units also differ: 201.51(b) allows metric or avoirdupois for Rx, while 201.62(b) requires avoirdupois pound/ounce and U.S. gallon units for OTC, with an optional metric statement under 201.62(p).
The row's focus label '201 Subpart A' is wrong: 201.62 is in Subpart C (OTC drugs), and 201.51 is in Subpart B.

explanation: 201.62 is the right section for OTC drugs and J's elements fit it. The question asks about drug labels generally, though, and prescription and insulin-containing drugs follow different rules under 201.51. A key that cites only 201.62 omits a governing section and presents OTC-only placement and prominence rules as universal.
proposed_corrected_answer: OTC drugs, 21 CFR 201.62: declaration on the principal display panel (duplicated on alternate PDPs), as a distinct item, generally within the bottom 30% of the panel. Weight, measure or numerical count (count for tablets and capsules). Avoirdupois and U.S. liquid units, with an optional metric statement. Conspicuous boldface type with minimum heights scaled to PDP area. Dual-unit rules for packages under 4 lb or 1 gal. Prescription and insulin-containing drugs, 21 CFR 201.51: label bears a net quantity declaration by weight, measure or numerical count (count for unit dosage forms), in metric or avoirdupois/U.S. units (medical-gas rules in (b)(1)-(4)), as a distinct item on the label, accurate and exclusive of wrappers. Both sections exempt ointment samples of 8 g or less.

question_interpretation: Who must register a drug establishment, when initial registration is due, when it must be renewed or updated, and what information it requires.

issues.detail: The renewal part of the question is governed by 21 CFR 207.29(b): registration information must be reviewed and updated annually between October 1 and December 31, with the first update in the year of initial registration if that registration is before October 1. The same window is in FD&C Act 510(b)(1). 207.29(a) adds 30-day expedited updates. G cites none of these, so 'annual renewal' in J has no supporting citation.

J describes registrants with the statutory wording ('manufacturing, preparation, propagation, compounding, or processing'). 207.17(a) is framed as manufacturers, repackers, relabelers and salvagers of domestic establishments, and of foreign establishments whose drugs are imported or offered for import. Private label distributors that do not also manufacture, repack, relabel or salvage need not register (207.17(b)). Exemptions are in 510(g) and 207.13. J omits all of these.

J says only 'initial registration timing'. 207.21 sets the timing: a domestic establishment must register no later than 5 calendar days after beginning operations, and a foreign establishment before its drug is imported or offered for import.

explanation: 207.17, 207.21 and 207.25 correctly govern who registers, initial timing and content. The question also asks about renewal, which is governed by 207.29 (annual review and update, October 1–December 31), and G omits it. J omits the specific 5-day and foreign-establishment timing and the private-label-distributor and exemption carve-outs.
proposed_corrected_answer: Who (207.17): manufacturers, repackers, relabelers and salvagers must register each domestic establishment, and each foreign establishment whose drugs are imported or offered for import. 'Manufacture' includes preparation, propagation, compounding and processing (207.1). Private label distributors that do not perform these operations need not register. Exemptions are in 510(g) and 207.13. When (207.21): domestic establishments no later than 5 calendar days after beginning to manufacture, repack, relabel or salvage; foreign establishments before the drug is imported or offered for import. Content (207.25): owner/operator, establishment names and addresses, registration number, UFI, operations, official contact, and for foreign establishments the U.S. agent and importers. Renewal (207.29): annual review and update between October 1 and December 31 (FD&C 510(b)), with 'no changes' certification allowed; expedited updates within 30 days for closure or sale, name or address change, or contact or agent change.

question_interpretation: What the drug listing requirements are (who lists, what, and when) and how the NDC is structured and assigned.

issues.detail: J asks for listing 'timing for submissions' but G cites no timing section. 21 CFR 207.45 requires listing no later than 3 calendar days after initial registration. 21 CFR 207.57 requires review and update each June and December, and listing of new drugs at annual registration.

207.49 covers only drugs the registrant manufactures. Repackers and relabelers list under 207.53 and salvagers under 207.54, and 207.41(b) points to all three. 207.35 (changes requiring a new NDC) is also relevant to 'how the NDC is assigned'.

Current 207.33(b) allows a 10- or 11-digit NDC: 4-, 5- or 6-digit labeler code, 3- or 4-digit product code, 1- or 2-digit package code, in configurations 4-4-2, 5-4-1, 5-3-2, 6-4-1 or 6-3-2. The labeler code is assigned by FDA, and FDA assigns the full NDC on receipt of conforming listing information (207.33(d)). The eCFR flags an amendment at 91 FR 10770 (FR Doc. 2026-04368) that will require a uniform 12-digit 6-4-2 NDC, effective March 7, 2033. Answers must state current law, and the key should note the future change.

explanation: 207.33 (NDC), 207.41 (who lists) and 207.49 (listing content for manufacturers) are correct. The key omits the listing-timing sections 207.45 and 207.57, which its own J element ('timing for submissions') depends on, and the repacker/relabeler content section 207.53. The NDC composition element is correct, but the answer should give the current 10/11-digit structure.
proposed_corrected_answer: NDC (207.33): unique numeric code identifying labeler, product and package. Currently 10 or 11 digits in three segments: labeler code of 4, 5 or 6 digits assigned by FDA on application under 207.33(c); product code of 3 or 4 digits; package code of 1 or 2 digits; permitted configurations 4-4-2, 5-4-1, 5-3-2, 6-4-1 and 6-3-2, with one product-package configuration per labeler code. The registrant proposes the NDC with its listing, FDA assigns it on receipt of conforming listing information, and a proposed NDC may be reserved for 2 years. 207.35 says when a new NDC is needed. A final rule (91 FR 10749) moves to a uniform 12-digit 6-4-2 format effective March 7, 2033. Listing (207.41): each registrant lists every drug it manufactures, repacks, relabels or salvages for commercial distribution, including private-label NDCs. Content: 207.49 (manufactured), 207.53 (repacked or relabeled), 207.54 (salvaged). Timing: 207.45, within 3 calendar days after initial registration; 207.57, updates each June and December and listing of new drugs at annual registration, with 'no changes' certification allowed.
